verification_scope: Official documentation was read through the page-fetch tool. These are specification checks, not claims of a successful authenticated live integration. Automated tests use synthetic fixtures and mocked network responses.

facts.fact: Recommended REST root is external-api.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2; demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2 is also supported. Recommended WebSocket root is external-api-ws.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2; demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2 is also supported.
Demo uses mock funds, has separate credentials, and its prices/behavior may not reflect production.
Timestamp milliseconds + uppercase HTTP method + full path without query; RSA-PSS SHA-256 with digest-length salt, or Ed25519; base64 signature and three KALSHI-ACCESS headers.
Even public market-data WebSocket channels require an authenticated handshake signed with GET /trade-api/ws/v2.
GET /events has a maximum limit of 200 and cursor pagination. with_nested_markets includes child markets but excludes archived markets.

Use series-level category, not deprecated event.category. Series include title, category, categories, tags and settlement_sources. Dashboard topic classification itself is a local rule, not an official fact.
Market REST responses are cached and can lag exchange state. Undecodable cursors may return the first page, requiring duplicate/loop protection.
Ticker dollar_volume is whole-dollar cumulative traded notional; dollar_open_interest is whole-dollar open-interest notional. These are not cash paid, and are not 24-hour amounts.
Ticker updates are coalesced on a roughly one-second schedule; intermediate prices are not all sent. The trade channel sends notifications after each execution.
Alert on an inclusive absolute YES last-price move of at least $0.10. This service uses a 60-second observed window and re-anchors after an alert; no interpolation or invented old history.
REST orderbook_fp contains yes_dollars and no_dollars price/quantity pairs. Both are bid books; asks are complementary opposite bids. Quantities are contracts, not order counts.
WebSocket snapshots use yes_dollars_fp/no_dollars_fp; deltas use price_dollars/delta_fp/side. seq is checked per subscription. Sequence gaps require fresh snapshots, not a repeated subscribe alone.

Order V2 uses bid/ask with a single YES price scale. Buying NO at cost q maps to ask at YES price 1-q. WebSocket orderbooks opt into YES pricing using use_yes_price=true; this service explicitly converts NO levels into its internal NO-leg book representation.

REST active is open; closed awaits determination; determined/disputed/amended are not final. REST finalized is terminal settlement. Filter settled maps to finalized. An event has no reliable top-level status and can contain children in different states.
Simple binary YES/NO winners receive $1 per contract. Scalar and settlement-bound contracts need distinct treatment and are not forced to binary in this service.
POST /portfolio/events/orders is the V2 order-write endpoint. Legacy /portfolio/orders writes have been removed and return 410. 201 means accepted, not necessarily filled/resting.

Upstream client_order_id uniqueness is limited to open orders in a subaccount/shard. Check acceptance before retrying after uncertainty; reusing an ID after fill/cancel is not durable exactly-once protection.
V2 cancellation requires market_ticker to auto-route to the correct shard; an order ID alone does not identify the shard.
Balance and portfolio_value integer fields are in cents; balance_dollars is a dollar string. Balance has a separate rate bucket. This service caches protected portfolio reads for 15 seconds.
Positions default to unsettled. settlement_status=all includes unarchived settled positions. position_fp is signed; realized_pnl_dollars and fees_paid_dollars are explicit API fields.
Fills are matched trades. Current responses include outcome_side/book_side, fixed-point counts, prices and fee_cost; legacy action/side are deprecated.
Settlement records include explicit market_result, fixed-point counts/cost, revenue in cents, fees and settlement time. This live endpoint does not return archived settlements.

Market candlesticks accept period_interval 1, 60 or 1440 minutes and Unix-second start/end timestamps. close_dollars may be null. Published candle/depth fallbacks retain their source timestamps, do not create alerts, and are never described as current liquidity.
GitHub Pages hosts static HTML/CSS/JavaScript. Private signing, durable account state and a continuous authenticated exchange stream require a separately hosted trusted backend.

Historical markets, fills, orders and positions are separate. Read live positions before archive positions; reads are not atomic, overlap is possible, and archive positions differ from settlement records.

flagged_for_review.detail: No Kalshi credentials are present. No authenticated demo order, fill, balance or WebSocket handshake has been verified. Account values are blank.

The sandbox process cannot reach Kalshi hosts. A page-fetch tool successfully read public exchange/status, but that is not a persistent backend connection. Polling/streaming require a host with Kalshi network access.
GitHub Pages is a static website host. Secure signing, private account access, persistence and background collection require this separately deployed trusted service.
Neither momentum nor mean reversion has validated out-of-sample net ROI. Fair value and gross edge are model outputs, not official data. No high-ROI guarantee is made.
Paper results are gross only. Fee types/multipliers and event overrides vary; no universal fee is assumed. Net ROI stays null.
No verified causal news links have been observed. Catalyst lists remain empty rather than assigning news stories to price jumps.
REST markets may not include dollar_volume. Ranking values remain null until reported WS notional arrives for all tracked child markets; partial discovery is visibly flagged.

The public Pages-to-demo-API CORS path has not been verified end to end. Local Chromium checks intentionally block or mock the exchange network. Direct REST failures retain source-timestamped observations; no synthetic prices replace them.

The bounded public snapshot contains no Culture contracts. On 2026-11-22 the two series returned by the official Culture category query were individually checked for open events and both returned empty. This is not proof of complete topic coverage; no substitute contracts are invented.
Five-topic classification uses explicit local metadata rules, not a verified full exchange taxonomy. Unmatched and ambiguous series are excluded and counted.
Portfolio collection is scoped to primary subaccount 0. It does not claim all subaccounts, atomic live/archive reconciliation, or cash-flow-adjusted ROI.
